    cleanStatusPath(path) {
      let value = (path || '').trim()
      if (value.includes(' -> ')) value = value.split(' -> ').pop()
      return value.replace(/^"|"$/g, '').trim()
    },

    statusMeta(code) {
      const meta = {
        A: { label: 'Added', icon: 'fa-circle-plus', color: 'text-success' },
        M: { label: 'Modified', icon: 'fa-pen', color: 'text-warning' },
        D: { label: 'Deleted', icon: 'fa-trash-can', color: 'text-error' },
        R: { label: 'Renamed', icon: 'fa-arrow-right-arrow-left', color: 'text-info' },
        C: { label: 'Copied', icon: 'fa-copy', color: 'text-info' },
        T: { label: 'Type changed', icon: 'fa-shuffle', color: 'text-warning' },
        U: { label: 'Conflict', icon: 'fa-triangle-exclamation', color: 'text-error' },
        '?': { label: 'Untracked', icon: 'fa-file-circle-plus', color: 'text-success' }
      }
      return meta[(code || '').trim()] || meta.M
    },

    /** Status code for an API entry, which can expose a code or a status name */
    codeFor(file) {
      if (file?.code) return file.code
      const codes = {
        added: 'A',
        modified: 'M',
        deleted: 'D',
        renamed: 'R',
        copied: 'C',
        typechange: 'T',
        conflict: 'U',
        untracked: '?'
      }
      return codes[(file?.status || '').toLowerCase()] || 'M'
    },

    buildStatusFile(code, path) {
      const clean = this.cleanStatusPath(path)
      if (!clean) return null
      const normalized = (code || '').trim() || 'M'
      const meta = this.statusMeta(normalized)
      return {
        path: clean,
        code: normalized,
        icon: meta.icon,
        color: meta.color,
        label: meta.label
      }
    },

    fileName(path) {
      return (path || '').split('/').pop()
    },

    fileDir(path) {
      const parts = (path || '').split('/')
      parts.pop()
      return parts.join('/')
    },

    isSectionCollapsed(key) {
      return !!this.collapsedSections[key]
    },

    toggleSection(key) {
      this.collapsedSections = {
        ...this.collapsedSections,
        [key]: !this.collapsedSections[key]
      }
    },

    // ── Multi selection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    fileKey(group, path) {
      return `${group}:${path}`
    },

    isSelected(group, path) {
      return !!this.selection[this.fileKey(group, path)]
    },

    /** Index of a file inside its group, -1 when it is not there anymore */
    fileIndex(group, path) {
      return this.groupFiles(group).findIndex(file => file.path === path)
    },

    /** Replace the whole selection with the given keys */
    setSelection(keys) {
      const next = {}
      ;(keys || []).forEach(key => { next[key] = true })
      this.selection = next
    },

    toggleSelect(group, path) {
      const key = this.fileKey(group, path)
      const next = { ...this.selection }
      if (next[key]) {
        delete next[key]
      } else {
        next[key] = true
      }
      this.selection = next
    },

    /**
     * Shift+click: select every file between the anchor and the clicked file.
     * Without a valid anchor in the same group it falls back to a single
     * selection.
     */
    selectRange(group, path) {
      const targetIndex = this.fileIndex(group, path)
      if (targetIndex < 0) return

      const anchor = this.selectionAnchor
      const anchorIndex = anchor && anchor.group === group
        ? this.fileIndex(group, anchor.path)
        : -1

      if (anchorIndex < 0) {
        this.setSelection([this.fileKey(group, path)])
        this.selectionAnchor = { group, path }
        return
      }

      const [start, end] = anchorIndex <= targetIndex
        ? [anchorIndex, targetIndex]
        : [targetIndex, anchorIndex]

      const files = this.groupFiles(group).slice(start, end + 1)
      this.setSelection(files.map(file => this.fileKey(group, file.path)))
    },

    /** Row click: plain = single selection + diff, ctrl = toggle, shift = range */
    onRowClick(event, group, file) {
      if (!file?.path) return

      if (event?.shiftKey) {
        this.selectRange(group, file.path)
        return
      }

      if (event?.ctrlKey || event?.metaKey) {
        this.toggleSelect(group, file.path)
      } else {
        this.setSelection([this.fileKey(group, file.path)])
      }

      this.selectionAnchor = { group, path: file.path }
      this.openDiff(group, file)
    },

    /** Checkbox click: plain = toggle, shift = select the range */
    onCheckboxClick(event, group, file) {
      if (!file?.path) return

      if (event?.shiftKey) {
        this.selectRange(group, file.path)
        return
      }

      this.toggleSelect(group, file.path)
      this.selectionAnchor = { group, path: file.path }
    },

    /** Paths of the current selection belonging to a group */
    selectedPaths(group) {
      const prefix = `${group}:`
      return Object.keys(this.selection)
        .filter(key => this.selection[key] && key.startsWith(prefix))
        .map(key => key.slice(prefix.length))
    },

    groupFiles(group) {
      return group === 'staged' ? this.stagedFiles : this.unstagedFiles
    },

    groupAllSelected(group) {
      const files = this.groupFiles(group)
      return files.length > 0 && files.every(file => this.isSelected(group, file.path))
    },

    toggleGroupSelection(group) {
      const files = this.groupFiles(group)
      const allSelected = this.groupAllSelected(group)
      const next = { ...this.selection }
      files.forEach(file => {
        const key = this.fileKey(group, file.path)
        if (allSelected) {
          delete next[key]
        } else {
          next[key] = true
        }
      })
      this.selection = next
    },

    clearSelection() {
      this.selection = {}
      this.selectionAnchor = null
    },

    /** Drop selections (and the anchor) whose file left its group */
    pruneSelection() {
      const valid = new Set()
      this.stagedFiles.forEach(file => valid.add(this.fileKey('staged', file.path)))
      this.unstagedFiles.forEach(file => valid.add(this.fileKey('changes', file.path)))
      const next = {}
      Object.keys(this.selection).forEach(key => {
        if (this.selection[key] && valid.has(key)) next[key] = true
      })
      this.selection = next

      if (this.selectionAnchor) {
        const anchorKey = this.fileKey(this.selectionAnchor.group, this.selectionAnchor.path)
        if (!valid.has(anchorKey)) this.selectionAnchor = null
      }
    },

    isFileOpen(group, path) {
      return this.selectedFile?.group === group && this.selectedFile?.path === path
    },

    openDiff(group, file) {
      if (!file?.path) return
      // Same file/group already open: keep it (no remount, no extra request)
      if (this.isFileOpen(group, file.path)) return
      this.selectedFile = {
        path: file.path,
        group,
        code: file.code,
        icon: file.icon,
        color: file.color,
        label: file.label
      }
    },

    closeDiff() {
      this.selectedFile = null
    },

    /** Keep the diff pane in sync with the reloaded working tree */
    syncSelectedFile() {
      if (!this.selectedFile) return

      const { path, group } = this.selectedFile
      const order = group === 'staged'
        ? ['staged', 'changes']
        : ['changes', 'staged']

      for (const key of order) {
        const match = this.groupFiles(key).find(file => file.path === path)
        if (match) {
          this.selectedFile = {
            path: match.path,
            group: key,
            code: match.code,
            icon: match.icon,
            color: match.color,
            label: match.label
          }
          return
        }
      }

      // The file is no longer part of the working tree (committed or rolled back)
      this.selectedFile = null
    },

    onFileChanged() {
      return this.loadRepo()
    },

    // ── Graph ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    onSelectCommit(commit) {
      this.selectedCommit = commit
    },

    closeCommit() {
      this.selectedCommit = null
    },

    /**
     * Branch action requested from the commit panel (which only lists the refs
     * pointing to the selected commit): checkout, merge into the current
     * branch, rebase the current branch onto it, or delete the branch.
     */
    async onCommitBranchAction({ action, branch } = {}) {
      if (!branch || !this.api) return

      if (action === 'checkout') {
        return this.onCheckout(branch)
      }

      if (action === 'delete') {
        await this.deleteBranch(branch)
        this.selectedCommit = null
        return
      }

      const target = this.currentBranch
      if (!target) {
        this.error = 'No branch is checked out'
        return
      }
      if (this.sameBranch(branch, target)) {
        this.error = `"${branch}" is already the current branch`
        return
      }

      if (action === 'merge') {
        const accepted = await this.confirmAction({
          title: 'Merge branch',
          message: `Merge "${branch}" into "${target}"?`,
          hint: 'A merge commit is created on the current branch. Nothing is pushed.',
          icon: 'fa-code-merge',
          iconClass: 'text-warning',
          confirmLabel: 'Merge',
          confirmIcon: 'fa-code-merge',
          confirmClass: 'btn-warning'
        })
        if (!accepted) return

        await this.runOperation(
          () => this.api.repo.merge({ from_branch: branch, to_branch: target }),
          `Merged ${branch} into ${target}`
        )
        this.selectedCommit = null
        return
      }

      if (action === 'rebase') {
        const accepted = await this.confirmAction({
          title: 'Rebase branch',
          message: `Rebase "${target}" onto "${branch}"?`,
          hint: 'Rebasing rewrites the commits of the current branch: their hashes change. Nothing is pushed.',
          icon: 'fa-arrows-rotate',
          iconClass: 'text-warning',
          confirmLabel: 'Rebase',
          confirmIcon: 'fa-arrows-rotate',
          confirmClass: 'btn-warning'
        })
        if (!accepted) return

        await this.runOperation(
          () => this.api.repo.rebase({ onto_branch: branch, branch: target }),
          `Rebased ${target} onto ${branch}`
        )
        this.selectedCommit = null
      }
    },

    // ── Working tree operations ─────────────────────────────────────────
    async stagePaths(paths) {
      const list = paths || []
      if (!list.length || !this.api) return
      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.stage(list),
        `${list.length} file(s) staged`
      )
      this.clearSelection()
    },

    async unstagePaths(paths) {
      const list = paths || []
      if (!list.length || !this.api) return
      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.unstage(list),
        `${list.length} file(s) unstaged`
      )
      this.clearSelection()
    },

    async discardPaths(paths) {
      const list = paths || []
      if (!list.length || !this.api) return

      const accepted = await this.confirmAction({
        title: 'Roll back changes',
        message: list.length === 1
          ? `Roll back "${list[0]}" to the last commit?`
          : `Roll back ${list.length} files to the last commit?`,
        details: list,
        hint: 'Tracked files are restored from the last commit. Untracked and newly added files are deleted. This cannot be undone.',
        icon: 'fa-rotate-left',
        iconClass: 'text-error',
        confirmLabel: 'Roll back',
        confirmIcon: 'fa-rotate-left',
        confirmClass: 'btn-error'
      })
      if (!accepted) return

      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.discard(list, true),
        `${list.length} file(s) rolled back`
      )
      this.clearSelection()
    },

    // ── Repository lock ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    /**
     * Remove the stale `.git/index.lock` after the user confirms it.
     *
     * The lock is only safe to release when no git process is running, so the
     * confirmation warns about it before deleting the file.
     */
    async releaseLock() {
      if (!this.api) return
      const accepted = await this.confirmAction({
        title: 'Release repository lock',
        message: 'Remove the git lock file and unlock the repository?',
        details: this.lockPath ? [this.lockPath] : [],
        hint: 'Only do this if no git process is running. Removing index.lock while git is writing can corrupt the repository.',
        icon: 'fa-lock-open',
        iconClass: 'text-warning',
        confirmLabel: 'Release lock',
        confirmIcon: 'fa-lock-open',
        confirmClass: 'btn-warning'
      })
      if (!accepted) return

      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.releaseLock(),
        'Repository lock released'
      )
    },

    // ── Loading ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    async loadRepo() {
      if (!this.api) return
      this.loading = true
      this.error = null
      try {
        const [info, branchesRes] = await Promise.all([
          this.api.repo.info().catch(() => ({})),
          this.api.repo.branches()
        ])
        this.info = info || {}
        this.branches = Array.isArray(branchesRes) ? branchesRes : (branchesRes?.branches || [])
        this.repoTree = branchesRes?.repo_tree || []

        if (!this.selectedBranch || !this.branches.includes(this.selectedBranch)) {
          this.selectedBranch = this.currentBranch || this.branches[0] || null
        }
        this.pruneSelection()
        this.syncSelectedFile()
        await this.loadCommitsForBranch(this.selectedBranch)
      } catch (ex) {
        this.error = `Unable to load repository: ${ex?.message || ex}`
      } finally {
        this.loading = false
      }
    },

    selectBranch(branch) {
      if (!branch) return
      this.selectedBranch = branch
      this.rawCommits = []
      this.loadCommitsForBranch(branch)
    },

    async loadCommitsForBranch(branch) {
      if (!this.api || !branch) return
      const tree = this.repoTree.find(b => this.sameBranch(b.branch_name, branch))
      if (tree?.commits?.length) {
        this.rawCommits = []
        return
      }
      this.commitsLoading = true
      try {
        const res = await this.api.repo.commits(branch)
        this.rawCommits = this.parseRawCommits(res)
      } catch {
        this.rawCommits = []
      } finally {
        this.commitsLoading = false
      }
    },

    /** Fallback parser for `git log` output when repo_tree is not available */
    parseRawCommits(res) {
      const raw = res?.commits ?? res
      if (Array.isArray(raw)) return raw.map(c => this.normalizeCommit(c))
      if (typeof raw !== 'string' || !raw.trim()) return []
      return raw.split(/^commit /m).filter(Boolean).map(block => {
        const lines = block.split('\n')
        const id = lines[0].trim().split(' ')[0]
        const authorLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('Author:')) || ''
        const dateLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('Date:')) || ''
        const blankIndex = lines.findIndex(l => l.trim() === '')
        const message = (blankIndex > -1 ? lines.slice(blankIndex + 1).join(' ') : '').trim()
        return this.normalizeCommit({
          commit: id,
          author: authorLine.replace('Author:', '').trim(),
          date: dateLine.replace('Date:', '').trim(),
          message
        })
      })
    },

    // ── Shared operation runner ─────────────────────────────────────────
    async runOperation(fn, successMessage) {
      if (!this.api) return
      this.error = null
      this.notice = null
      this.busy = true
      try {
        const result = await fn()
        const errors = (result && Array.isArray(result.errors) ? result.errors : []).filter(Boolean)
        // Some endpoints answer 200 with success:false (e.g. stage): never
        // report them as succeeded
        if (result && result.success === false) {
          throw new Error(errors.join('; ') || 'Git operation failed')
        }
        if (successMessage) this.notice = successMessage
        await this.loadRepo()
        // Branches, hashes and lanes changed: reload the graph too
        this.graphRefreshToken += 1
        return result
      } catch (ex) {
        this.error = ex?.response?.data?.detail || ex?.message || String(ex)
        // Reflect whatever could be applied (e.g. a partial staging)
        await this.loadRepo()
        this.graphRefreshToken += 1
      } finally {
        this.busy = false
      }
    },

    // ── Remote operations ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    onFetch() {
      this.runOperation(() => this.api.repo.fetch(), 'Fetched from remote')
    },
    onPull() {
      this.runOperation(() => this.api.repo.pull(), 'Pulled from remote')
    },
    onPush() {
      this.runOperation(() => this.api.repo.push(), 'Pushed to remote')
    },

    // ── Branch operations ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    onCheckout(branch) {
      if (!branch || this.sameBranch(branch, this.currentBranch)) return
      this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.checkoutBranch(branch),
        `Checked out ${branch}`
      )
    },

    /** Open the create-branch modal, pre-filling the base branch */
    openNewBranch(from = '') {
      this.newBranchName = ''
      this.newBranchCheckout = false
      this.newBranchFrom = from || this.selectedBranch || this.currentBranch || ''
      this.showNewBranch = true
    },

    closeNewBranch() {
      this.showNewBranch = false
      this.newBranchName = ''
      this.newBranchCheckout = false
    },

    async createBranch() {
      const name = this.newBranchName.trim()
      if (!name || !this.api) return
      const from = this.newBranchFrom || this.currentBranch || ''
      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.createBranch({
          branch: name,
          from_branch: from,
          checkout: this.newBranchCheckout
        }),
        `Branch ${name} created from ${from}`
      )
      if (!this.error) {
        this.closeNewBranch()
        this.selectedBranch = name
        this.loadCommitsForBranch(name)
      }
    },

    async deleteBranch(branch) {
      if (!branch || !this.api) return

      const accepted = await this.confirmAction({
        title: 'Delete branch',
        message: `Delete branch "${branch}"?`,
        hint: 'The branch is removed locally. Commits that are not reachable from another branch are lost.',
        icon: 'fa-trash',
        iconClass: 'text-error',
        confirmLabel: 'Delete branch',
        confirmIcon: 'fa-trash',
        confirmClass: 'btn-error'
      })
      if (!accepted) return

      await this.runOperation(
        () => this.api.repo.deleteBranch(branch),
        `Branch ${branch} deleted`
      )
    },

    // ── Commit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    async doCommit() {
      const message = this.commitMessage.trim()
      if (!message || !this.api || this.committing || !this.workingTreeCount) return
      // Commit what is staged; stage everything only when nothing is staged
      const stageAll = this.stagedFiles.length === 0
      this.committing = true
      this.error = null
      this.notice = null
      try {
        await this.api.repo.commit({ message, stage_all: stageAll })
        this.notice = 'Changes committed'
        this.commitMessage = ''
        this.clearSelection()
        await this.loadRepo()
        this.graphRefreshToken += 1
      } catch (ex) {
        this.error = ex?.response?.data?.detail || ex?.message || String(ex)
      } finally {
        this.committing = false
      }
    },

    // ── Merge ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    openMerge() {
      this.mergeFrom = this.selectedBranch || this.currentBranch || ''
      this.mergeTo = this.currentBranch || this.branches[0] || ''
      this.mergeMessage = ''
      this.mergePreview = null
      this.showMerge = true
      this.loadMergePreview()
    },

    async loadMergePreview() {
      if (!this.api || !this.mergeFrom || !this.mergeTo) return
      this.mergePreviewLoading = true
      this.mergePreview = null
      try {
        const changes = await this.api.repo.changes({
          from_branch: this.mergeFrom,
          to_branch: this.mergeTo
        })
        const files = Object.keys(changes?.branch_file_and_commits || {})
        this.mergePreview = {
          fileCount: files.length,
          files: files.slice(0, 25),
          stat: changes?.stat || ''
        }
      } catch {
        this.mergePreview = null
      } finally {
        this.mergePreviewLoading = false
      }
    },

    async doMerge() {
      if (!this.mergeFrom || !this.mergeTo || !this.api) return
      if (this.sameBranch(this.mergeFrom, this.mergeTo)) {
        this.error = 'Source and target branches must be different'
        return
      }
      this.merging = true
      this.error = null
      try {
        await this.api.repo.merge({
          from_branch: this.mergeFrom,
          to_branch: this.mergeTo,
          message: this.mergeMessage.trim() || undefined
        })
        this.notice = `Merged ${this.mergeFrom} into ${this.mergeTo}`
        this.showMerge = false
        await this.loadRepo()
        this.graphRefreshToken += 1
      } catch (ex) {
        this.error = ex?.response?.data?.detail || ex?.message || String(ex)
      } finally {
        this.merging = false
      }
    }
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="git-view h-full w-full flex flex-col bg-base-100 overflow-hidden">
    <!-- ── Toolbar ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
    <header class="flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 bg-base-200 border-b border-base-content/10 shrink-0 flex-wrap">
      <i class="fa-solid fa-folder-tree text-warning"></i>
      <span class="font-mono text-sm font-semibold truncate min-w-0" :title="projectPath">{{ projectName }}</span>
      <span
        v-if="currentBranch"
        class="badge badge-sm badge-primary badge-outline gap-1 max-w-[220px]"
        :title="`Current branch: ${currentBranch}`"
      >
        <i class="fa-solid fa-check text-[9px] shrink-0"></i>
        <span class="truncate">{{ currentBranch }}</span>
      </span>

      <div class="grow"></div>

      <div v-if="isGit" class="join">
        <button class="join-item btn btn-xs btn-ghost" @click="onFetch" :disabled="busy" title="Fetch from remote">
          <i class="fa-solid fa-cloud-arrow-down"></i>
        </button>
        <button class="join-item btn btn-xs btn-ghost" @click="onPull" :disabled="busy" title="Pull from remote">
          <i class="fa-solid fa-arrow-down"></i>
        </button>
        <button class="join-item btn btn-xs btn-ghost" @click="onPush" :disabled="busy" title="Push to remote">
          <i class="fa-solid fa-arrow-up"></i>
        </button>
      </div>

      <button class="btn btn-xs btn-ghost" @click="loadRepo" :disabled="loading" title="Reload repository">
        <i class="fa-solid fa-rotate-right" :class="{ 'animate-spin': loading }"></i>
      </button>

      <div class="join">
        <button
          class="join-item btn btn-xs"
          :class="activeTab === 'repository' ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-ghost'"
          @click="activeTab = 'repository'"
          title="Working tree, branches and commits"
        >
          <i class="fa-solid fa-code-branch"></i> Repository
        </button>
        <button
          class="join-item btn btn-xs"
          :class="activeTab === 'graph' ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-ghost'"
          @click="activeTab = 'graph'"
          title="Commit graph of every branch"
        >
          <i class="fa-solid fa-diagram-project"></i> Graph
        </button>
        <button
          class="join-item btn btn-xs"
          :class="activeTab === 'review' ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-ghost'"
          @click="activeTab = 'review'"
          title="Compare branches and review diffs"
        >
          <i class="fa-solid fa-code-compare"></i> Review
        </button>
      </div>
    </header>

    <!-- ── Feedback ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
    <div v-if="error" class="alert alert-error rounded-none py-1 px-3 text-xs flex items-center gap-2 shrink-0">
      <i class="fa-solid fa-triangle-exclamation"></i>
      <span class="grow">{{ error }}</span>
      <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-xs" @click="error = null" aria-label="Dismiss error">
        <i class="fa-solid fa-xmark"></i>
      </button>
    </div>
    <div v-if="notice" class="alert alert-success rounded-none py-1 px-3 text-xs flex items-center gap-2 shrink-0">
      <i class="fa-solid fa-circle-check"></i>
      <span class="grow">{{ notice }}</span>
      <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-xs" @click="notice = null" aria-label="Dismiss notice">
        <i class="fa-solid fa-xmark"></i>
      </button>
    </div>

    <!-- ── Repository locked (stale .git/index.lock) ─────────────────────── -->
    <div v-if="locked" class="alert alert-warning rounded-none py-1 px-3 text-xs flex items-center gap-2 shrink-0">
      <i class="fa-solid fa-lock"></i>
      <span class="grow truncate" :title="lockPath ? `Locked by ${lockPath}` : 'Repository locked'">

<script>
export default {
  name: 'GitGraph',
  props: {
    // Project API instance (the graph is scoped by the project codx_path)
    api: { type: Object, required: true },
    // Branches offered by the branch filter
    branches: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
    currentBranch: { type: String, default: '' },
    defaultBranch: { type: String, default: '' },
    // Bumped by the parent view after a git operation to reload the graph
    refreshToken: { type: Number, default: 0 }
  },
  emits: ['select-commit'],
  data() {
    return {
      loading: false,
      error: null,
      // Normalized commits of the whole repository (before filtering)
      rawCommits: [],
      rows: [],
      laneCount: 1,
      branchFilter: '',
      showRemote: true,
      search: '',
      limit: 150,
      selectedHash: null,
      rowHeight: GRAPH_ROW_HEIGHT,
      laneSpacing: GRAPH_LANE_WIDTH
    }
  },
  computed: {
    graphWidth() {
      return Math.max(this.laneCount, 1) * this.laneSpacing + 12
    },
    branchOptions() {
      return this.branches
        .filter(branch => this.showRemote || !/^(origin|upstream)\//.test(branch))
        .sort((a, b) => (a > b ? 1 : -1))
    },
    searchTerm() {
      return this.search.trim().toLowerCase()
    }
  },
  watch: {
    api: {
      immediate: false,
      handler() {
        this.load()
      }
    },
    branchFilter() {
      this.applyFilter()
    },
    showRemote() {
      // A selected remote branch may disappear from the filter options
      if (this.branchFilter && !this.branchOptions.includes(this.branchFilter)) {
        this.branchFilter = ''
      }
      // Remote commits are only returned when requested
      this.load()
    },
    // Checkout, merge or rebase: the lanes and hashes change
    currentBranch() {
      this.load()
    },
    refreshToken() {
      this.load()
    }
  },
  created() {
    this.load()
  },
  methods: {
    // ── Loading ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    async load() {
      if (!this.api?.repo?.graph) {
        this.error = 'Repository API not available'
        return
      }
      this.loading = true
      this.error = null
      try {
        const graph = await this.api.repo.graph({ limit: this.limit, includeRemote: this.showRemote })
        this.rawCommits = graph?.commits || []
        this.applyFilter()
      } catch (ex) {
        this.rawCommits = []
        this.rows = []
        this.laneCount = 1
        this.error = ex?.response?.data?.detail || ex?.message || String(ex)
      } finally {
        this.loading = false
      }
    },

    /** Re-lay out the rows for the current branch filter */
    applyFilter() {
      const commits = this.branchFilter
        ? filterCommitsByRef(this.rawCommits, this.branchFilter)
        : this.rawCommits
      const layout = buildGraphLayout(commits)
      this.rows = layout.rows
      this.laneCount = layout.laneCount
      const stillThere = commits.some(commit => commit.hash === this.selectedHash)
      if (!stillThere) this.selectedHash = null
    },

    // ── Geometry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    laneX(lane) {
      return 8 + Math.max(Number(lane) || 0, 0) * this.laneSpacing
    },

    /**
     * Turn the row edges into SVG paths. A same-lane edge is a straight line,
     * a lane change becomes a smooth bezier so branches curve like in VSCode.
     */
    rowEdges(row) {
      const height = this.rowHeight
      return (row.edges || []).map(edge => {
        const x1 = this.laneX(edge.fromLane)
        const x2 = this.laneX(edge.toLane)
        const y1 = edge.fromY * height
        const y2 = edge.toY * height
        if (x1 === x2) {
          return { d: `M ${x1} ${y1} L ${x1} ${y2}`, color: edge.color }
        }
        const curve = (y2 - y1) * 0.5
        return {
          d: `M ${x1} ${y1} C ${x1} ${y1 + curve} ${x2} ${y2 - curve} ${x2} ${y2}`,
          color: edge.color
        }
      })
    },

    // ── Refs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    visibleRefs(refs) {
      return (refs || []).filter(ref => {
        if (ref.type === 'head') return true
        if (!this.showRemote) return ref.type !== 'remote'
        return true
      })
    },

    refClass(ref) {
      const styles = {
        local: 'badge-success',
        remote: 'badge-info badge-outline',
        tag: 'badge-warning badge-outline',
        head: 'badge-success'
      }
      return styles[ref.type] || 'badge-ghost'
    },

    refIcon(ref) {
      const icons = {
        local: 'fa-code-branch',
        remote: 'fa-cloud',
        tag: 'fa-tag',
        head: 'fa-check'
      }
      return icons[ref.type] || 'fa-code-branch'
    },

    // ── Row state ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    isDimmed(row) {
      if (!this.searchTerm) return false
      const { subject, short, hash, author } = row.commit
      return ![subject, short, hash, author?.name].some(value =>
        String(value || '').toLowerCase().includes(this.searchTerm)
      )
    },

    formatDate(date) {
      const value = moment(date)
      return value.isValid() ? value.format('DD MMM YYYY HH:mm') : (date || '')
    },

    selectRow(row) {
      this.selectedHash = row.commit.hash
      this.$emit('select-commit', row.commit)
    }
  }
}
</script>

    },

      const parent = this.commit?.parents?.[0]
      return parent ? parent.slice(0, 8) : ''
    },

    },

    },

      this.loading = true
      this.error = null
      this.stat = ''
      this.files = []
      this.selectedPath = ''
      this.diff = ''

      try {

        this.files = detail?.files || []
        if (this.files.length) {

      this.diffError = null
      try {
        const payload = await this.api.repo.fileDiff({
          path: this.selectedPath,
          mode: 'commit',
          commit: this.commit?.hash
        })
        this.diff = payload?.diff || ''
      } catch (ex) {

      } finally {

    statusColor(status) {

        new: 'text-success',
        deleted: 'text-error',
        renamed: 'text-info',
        copied: 'text-info',
        modified: 'text-warning'
      }
      return colors[status] || colors.modified
    },

    refClass(ref) {

        remote: 'badge-info badge-outline',
        tag: 'badge-warning badge-outline'

        remote: 'fa-cloud',
        tag: 'fa-tag'
      }
      return icons[ref.type] || 'fa-code-branch'
    },

    formatDate(date) {
      const value = moment(date)
      return value.isValid() ? value.format('DD MMM YYYY HH:mm') : (date || '')
    }
  }
}
</script>

I'll first investigate how project settings and git identity are handled today.## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking

**Core requirement**
- Repository writes performed by codx-junior (commits, merges, rebases, PR branches) must be signed with the **project's** configured git user name/email, not only with the installation-wide identity.

**Current behaviour (findings)**
- `CODXJuniorSettings` (`codx/junior/settings.py`) has **no git identity fields** — only `git_pr_branch_prefix` / `git_worktrees_path`.
- The only identity is `GlobalSettings.git` (`GitSettings.username/email`), applied once through `git config --global` when global settings are written (`codx/junior/global_settings.py`).
- `GitEngine._run_git()` (`codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py`) is the single choke point for every git call made by `GitEngine`, `GitWorkspaceEngine` and `GitGraphEngine` (commit, merge, rebase, stash, worktree…) — but it forwards no identity.

**Strategy**
1. Add `git_user_name` / `git_user_email` to the project settings (persisted automatically through `get_valid_keys()`).
2. In `GitEngine`: resolve identity with fallback chain **project settings → global settings → repo `git config`** (cached), and inject it into every git command as `git -c user.name=… -c user.email=…` — this signs commits/merges/rebases/cherry-picks without mutating `.git/config`.
3. Expose the resolved identity in `get_repo_info()` so the UI can show who authors the commits.

**Risks / edge cases**
- Recursion: identity resolution must not re-enter `_run_git` with identity applied → `apply_identity` flag + cache.
- Empty settings must never blank a correctly configured repo identity → fallback to `git config`.
- Read-only commands are unaffected by `-c user.name/user.email`.

**Target files**
- `codx/junior/settings.py` (modify)
- `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py` (modify)

| `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py` | Add identity resolution (`get_git_identity`), `-c` injection in `_run_git`, identity cache in `__init__`, identity in `get_repo_info`. |

        Keeps the last part after splitting by space.
        
        Args:
            branch: Raw branch name that may contain prefixes.
            
        Returns:
            Cleaned branch name.
        """
        if not branch:
            return branch
        
        # Remove common git branch prefixes
        cleaned = branch.lstrip("* +").strip()
        
        # If there's still a space, take the last part (handles "worktree/branch" cases)
        if " " in cleaned:
            cleaned = cleaned.split()[-1]
        
        return cleaned

    def _get_repo_root(self) -> str:
        """
        Return the git root path for the project, falling back to the project path.

        Returns:
            Absolute path of the repository root.
        """
        return self.find_git_root_path() or self.settings.abs_project_path

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Git identity (project settings -> global settings -> git config)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _configured_identity(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Return the git identity stored in the project and global settings.

        The project values (`git_user_name` / `git_user_email`) win over the
        global ones (`git.username` / `git.email`), so a single project can
        commit with a different author than the rest of the installation.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'name', 'email' and 'source' ('project', 'global' or an
            empty string when nothing is configured).

        Example:
            >>> engine._configured_identity()
            {'name': 'Jane Doe', 'email': 'jane@acme.com', 'source': 'project'}
        """
        name = str(getattr(self.settings, "git_user_name", "") or "").strip()
        email = str(getattr(self.settings, "git_user_email", "") or "").strip()
        source = "project" if (name or email) else ""

        if name and email:
            return {"name": name, "email": email, "source": source}

        # Fall back to the global settings (installation wide identity)
        global_git = None
        try:
            from codx.junior.global_settings import get_global_settings

            global_git = getattr(get_global_settings(), "git", None)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("Could not read the global git settings: %s", ex)

        global_name = str(getattr(global_git, "username", "") or "").strip()
        global_email = str(getattr(global_git, "email", "") or "").strip()

        if not name and global_name:
            name = global_name
            source = source or "global"
        if not email and global_email:
            email = global_email
            source = source or "global"

        return {"name": name, "email": email, "source": source}

    def _git_config_identity(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Read `user.name` and `user.email` from the repository git configuration.

        Used as the last fallback, so an identity already configured for the
        repository is never wiped by empty project settings. The git calls skip
        the identity override, otherwise resolving the identity would require
        the identity itself.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'name' and 'email' (empty strings when not configured).
        """
        name = self._run_git(["config", "--get", "user.name"], apply_identity=False)
        email = self._run_git(["config", "--get", "user.email"], apply_identity=False)
        return {
            "name": name["output"] if name["ok"] else "",
            "email": email["output"] if email["ok"] else "",
        }

    def get_git_identity(self, refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
        """
        Return the identity every repository operation is signed with.

        Resolution order:
            1. project settings (`git_user_name` / `git_user_email`)
            2. global settings (`git.username` / `git.email`)
            3. the git configuration (`user.name` / `user.email`)

        The result is cached: it is applied to every git command.

        Args:
            refresh: Re-read the settings instead of returning the cache.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'name', 'email' and 'source' ('project', 'global',
            'git-config' or '' when the identity is unknown).

        Example:
            >>> engine.get_git_identity()["email"]
            'jane@acme.com'
        """
        if self._git_identity and not refresh:
            return dict(self._git_identity)

        identity = self._configured_identity()
        if not identity["name"] or not identity["email"]:
            config_identity = self._git_config_identity()
            if not identity["name"]:
                identity["name"] = config_identity["name"]
            if not identity["email"]:
                identity["email"] = config_identity["email"]
            if not identity["source"] and (identity["name"] or identity["email"]):
                identity["source"] = "git-config"

        self._git_identity = identity
        return dict(identity)

    def _identity_args(self) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the `-c` overrides that sign a git command with the identity.

        ``-c user.name=... -c user.email=...`` must be placed before the
        subcommand: every git command that records an author or a committer
        (commit, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, tag) then uses it, without changing
        the repository or the global git configuration.

        Returns:
            Git argument list, empty when no identity is configured.

        Example:
            >>> engine._identity_args()
            ['-c', 'user.name=Jane Doe', '-c', 'user.email=jane@acme.com']
        """
        identity = self.get_git_identity()
        args: List[str] = []
        if identity["name"]:
            args += ["-c", f"user.name={identity['name']}"]
        if identity["email"]:
            args += ["-c", f"user.email={identity['email']}"]
        return args

    def _run_git(
        self,
        args: List[str],
        cwd: Optional[str] = None,
        strip_output: bool = True,
        apply_identity: bool = True,
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Run a git command without a shell and return a structured result.

        Uses ``subprocess.run`` with an argument list so branch names and file
        paths never need shell quoting, and stdout/stderr stay separated (unlike
        ``exec_command``, which merges stderr into stdout).

        The project git identity (see ``get_git_identity``) is passed as
        ``-c user.name`` / ``-c user.email``, so every commit, merge or rebase
        performed by the engine is signed with the project author.

        Args:
            args: Git arguments, e.g. ``["checkout", "-b", "feature/x"]``.
            cwd: Working directory. Defaults to the repository root.
            strip_output: Strip leading/trailing whitespace from stdout. Set it
                to False for commands whose leading spaces carry meaning, such
                as ``git status --porcelain``.
            apply_identity: Inject the git identity overrides (disable it while
                resolving the identity itself).

        Returns:
            Dict with 'ok', 'command', 'output', 'error' and 'returncode'.
        """
        cwd = cwd or self._get_repo_root()
        identity_args = self._identity_args() if apply_identity else []
        command = ["git"] + identity_args + list(args)
        command_str = " ".join(command)
        logger.info("git command: %s (cwd=%s)", command_str, cwd)
        try:
            completed = subprocess.run(
                command, cwd=cwd, text=True, capture_output=True
            )
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.error("Error running '%s': %s", command_str, ex)
            return {
                "ok": False,
                "command": command_str,
                "output": "",
                "error": str(ex),
                "returncode": -1,
            }

        raw_output = completed.stdout or ""
        output = raw_output.strip() if strip_output else raw_output
        error = (completed.stderr or "").strip()
        ok = completed.returncode == 0
        if not ok:
            logger.warning("git command failed: %s. %s", command_str, error)
        return {
            "ok": ok,
            "command": command_str,
            "output": output,
            "error": error,
            "returncode": completed.returncode,
        }

    def _ref_exists(self, ref: str, cwd: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        """
        Check whether a git ref (branch, remote branch or commit) exists.

        Args:
            ref: Full ref name, e.g. ``refs/heads/main`` or ``origin/main``.
            cwd: Working directory. Defaults to the repository root.

        Returns:
            True when the ref can be resolved.
        """
        result = self._run_git(["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref], cwd=cwd)
        return bool(result["ok"] and result["output"])

    def _resolve_base_ref(self, base_branch: Optional[str], cwd: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Resolve the ref a new PR branch should be created from.

        Local branches are preferred (PRs are reviewed locally) and the remote
        tracking branch is used as a fallback.

        Args:
            base_branch: Base branch name, may be empty.
            cwd: Working directory (repository root).

        Returns:
            Resolvable ref name, or None when the base branch is unknown.
        """
        if not base_branch:
            return None

        base_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(base_branch)
        for candidate in (
            f"refs/heads/{base_branch}",
            f"refs/remotes/origin/{base_branch}",
        ):
            if self._ref_exists(candidate, cwd=cwd):
                return candidate

        logger.warning("Base branch not found: %s", base_branch)
        return None

    def _get_remote_url(self, remote: str = DEFAULT_REMOTE) -> str:
        """
        Return the configured URL for a remote.

        Args:
            remote: Remote name.

        Returns:
            Remote URL, or an empty string when the remote is not configured.
        """
        result = self._run_git(["config", "--get", f"remote.{remote}.url"])
        return result["output"] if result["ok"] else ""

    def _get_ahead_behind(
        self, branch: str, remote: str = DEFAULT_REMOTE
    ) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """
        Return how many commits the local branch is ahead/behind its remote.

        Args:
            branch: Local branch name.
            remote: Remote name.

        Returns:
            Tuple of ``(ahead, behind)``; ``(0, 0)`` when there is no upstream.
        """
        if not branch:
            return 0, 0

        upstream = f"{remote}/{branch}"
        if not self._ref_exists(f"refs/remotes/{upstream}"):
            return 0, 0

        result = self._run_git(
            ["rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", f"{upstream}...{branch}"]
        )
        if not result["ok"] or not result["output"]:
            return 0, 0

        try:
            behind, ahead = result["output"].split()
        except ValueError:
            return 0, 0
        return int(ahead), int(behind)

    def _ensure_local_branch(
        self, branch: str, remote: str = DEFAULT_REMOTE
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Make sure a branch exists locally, creating it from the remote if needed.

        Args:
            branch: Branch name.
            remote: Remote name.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'ok', 'created' and 'error'.
        """
        if self._ref_exists(f"refs/heads/{branch}"):
            return {"ok": True, "created": False, "error": ""}

        if self._ref_exists(f"refs/remotes/{remote}/{branch}"):
            result = self._run_git(
                ["checkout", "-b", branch, f"{remote}/{branch}"]
            )
            return {
                "ok": result["ok"],
                "created": result["ok"],
                "error": result["error"],
            }

        return {
            "ok": False,
            "created": False,
            "error": f"Branch '{branch}' does not exist",
        }

    def _git_operation_result(self, command_result: dict, **extra) -> dict:
        """
        Convert a ``_run_git`` result into an operation result dict.

        Failures caused by a stale index lock are flagged with 'locked' and
        'lock_path' so the caller can offer to release the lock.

        Args:
            command_result: Dict returned by ``_run_git``.
            extra: Additional fields merged into the result.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'success', 'command', 'output' and 'errors'.
        """
        ok = bool(command_result.get("ok"))
        error = command_result.get("error") or ""
        result = {
            "success": ok,
            "command": command_result.get("command", ""),
            "output": command_result.get("output", ""),
            "errors": [] if ok else [error or "git command failed"],
            **extra,
        }
        if not ok:
            result.update(self._lock_error_info(error))
        return result

    def _git_operation_error(self, message: str, **extra) -> dict:
        """
        Build a failed operation result dict.

        Args:
            message: Human readable error message.
            extra: Additional fields merged into the result.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'success' set to False and the message in 'errors'.
        """
        return {"success": False, "errors": [message], **extra}

    def _lock_error_info(self, error_text: str) -> dict:
        """
        Detect a stale index lock in a failed git command output.

        Git refuses to write the index while ``.git/index.lock`` exists and
        reports ``Unable to create '.../index.lock': File exists``. Such a
        failure is returned with 'locked' and 'lock_path' so the UI can offer to
        release the lock instead of showing an opaque git error.

        Args:
            error_text: Stderr of the failed git command.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'locked' and 'lock_path' when the command failed because
            of the index lock, an empty dict otherwise.
        """
        text = (error_text or "").lower()
        lock_blocked = "index.lock" in text and (
            "file exists" in text or "unable to create" in text
        )
        if not lock_blocked:
            return {}
        info = self.get_lock_info()
        return {"locked": True, "lock_path": info.get("path", "")}

    def _get_file_last_modification(self, file_path: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Return the last modification datetime of a file as an ISO 8601 string.
        """
        if not os.path.isabs(file_path):
            file_path = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, file_path)
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            return None
        mtime = os.path.getmtime(file_path)
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(mtime).isoformat()

    def _get_git_root_for_file(self, file_path: str) -> str:
        """
        Determine the Git root for a given file, allowing for subprojects.

        Args:
            file_path: The path to the file.

        Returns:
            The absolute Git root path.
        """
        if not os.path.isabs(file_path):
            file_path = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, file_path)
            
        current_path = os.path.dirname(file_path)
        
        while current_path != os.path.dirname(current_path):
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(current_path, '.git')):
                return current_path
            current_path = os.path.dirname(current_path)
            
        return self.find_git_root_path()

    def _write_repo_file(self, repo_path: str, file_path: str, content: str) -> dict:
        """
        Write a file inside a repository (or worktree), creating parent folders.

        Paths escaping the repository root are rejected.

        Args:
            repo_path: Absolute repository (or worktree) root.
            file_path: Relative (to the repo) or absolute file path.
            content: Full file content to write.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'ok', 'file_path' (repo-relative) and 'error'.
        """
        repo_root = os.path.normpath(repo_path)
        resolved = file_path
        if not os.path.isabs(resolved):
            resolved = os.path.join(repo_root, resolved)
        resolved = os.path.normpath(resolved)

        if not resolved.startswith(repo_root + os.sep):
            return {
                "ok": False,
                "file_path": file_path,
                "error": f"File path must belong to {repo_path}",
            }

        try:
            dir_name = os.path.dirname(resolved)
            if dir_name:
                os.makedirs(dir_name, exist_ok=True)
            with open(resolved, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(content if content is not None else "")
        except (IOError, OSError) as ex:
            logger.error("Error writing file %s: %s", resolved, ex)
            return {"ok": False, "file_path": file_path, "error": str(ex)}

        return {
            "ok": True,
            "file_path": os.path.relpath(resolved, repo_root),
            "error": "",
        }

    def diff_file(self, path: str, content: str, from_branch: str = None, to_branch: str = None) -> dict:
        """
        Diff a project file against provided content using git diff --no-index.
        Optionally compare against specific branches.

        Args:
            path: File path.
            content: New content to diff against.
            from_branch: Optional source branch for comparison (git diff --no-index ignores this for file diffs).
            to_branch: Optional target branch for comparison (git diff --no-index ignores this for file diffs).

        Returns:
            Dict with 'diff', 'stats', 'last_modification', and 'size'.
        
        Note:
            For branch-based diffs, use git commands like:
            `git diff from_branch to_branch -- path` instead of `git diff --no-index`.
            This implementation uses --no-index for comparing working tree against provided content.
        """
        path = self._get_git_root_for_file(file_path=path)

        # For comparing against branches, we would use different git commands
        # Currently using --no-index for comparing working file against new content
        if from_branch and to_branch:
            # Compare file between two branches
            cmd = ["git", "diff", f"{from_branch}..{to_branch}", "--", path]
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            diff_out = result.stdout
            
            git_stats_cmd = ["git", "diff", f"{from_branch}..{to_branch}", "--shortstat", "--", path]
            stats_result = subprocess.run(git_stats_cmd, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            diff_stats_out = stats_result.stdout
        else:
            # Default behavior: compare provided content against current file
            cmd = ["git", "diff", "--no-index", path, "-"]
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, input=content, text=True, capture_output=True)
            diff_out = result.stdout

            git_command = f"""
            cat << EOF | git --no-pager diff --shortstat --no-index -- - {path}
            {content}
            EOF
            """
            diff_stats_out = os.popen(git_command).read()

        return {
            "diff": diff_out.strip(),
            "stats": diff_stats_out.strip(),
        }

    def get_repo_branches(self) -> list:
        """
        Return all git branches (local and remote) for the project.
        Sanitizes branch names by removing prefixes.
        """
        def get_branches(cmd: str) -> list:
            stdout, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            branches = [s.strip() for s in stdout.split("\n") if s.strip()]
            return [self._sanitize_branch_name(b) for b in branches]

        branches = list(set(get_branches("git branch") + get_branches("git branch -r")))
        branches.sort()
        return branches

    def get_project_branches(self) -> dict:
        """
        Return branches and full repo tree.
        """
        return {
            "branches": self.get_repo_branches(),
            "repo_tree": self.get_repo_tree(),
        }

    def get_project_branch_commits(self, branch: str) -> dict:
        """
        Return commits for a given branch.
        """
        branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(branch)
        commits, _ = exec_command(
            f"git log {branch}", cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
        )
        return {"commits": commits}

    def find_git_root_path(self) -> str:
        """
        Find the root path of the git repository by checking parents.
        """
        if self.settings.is_git_root:
            return self.settings.abs_project_path
        for parent in find_project_parents(project=self.settings):
            if parent.is_git_root:
                return parent.abs_project_path
        return ""

    def get_commit_list(self, branch: str = None, limit: int = 50) -> list:
        """
        Return a structured list of commits for a branch or HEAD.

        Args:
            branch: Branch name. Defaults to current HEAD.
            limit:  Maximum number of commits to return.

        Returns:
            List of commit dicts with hash, author, date, message.
        """
        if branch:
            branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(branch)
        
        ref = branch or "HEAD"
        pretty = "%H|%an|%ae|%ad|%s"
        cmd = f"git log --pretty=format:{pretty} --date=iso -n {limit} {ref}"
        stdout, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)

        commits = []
        for line in stdout.strip().split("\n"):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            try:
                commit_hash, author_name, author_email, date, message = line.split("|", 4)
                commits.append({
                    "commit": commit_hash,
                    "short_commit": commit_hash[:8],
                    "author": {"name": author_name, "email": author_email},
                    "date": date.strip(),
                    "message": message.strip(),
                    "label": f"{commit_hash[:8]} - {message.strip()[:60]}"
                })
            except ValueError:
                logger.warning("Could not parse commit line: %s", line)
        return commits

    def get_commit_changes(self, from_commit: str, to_commit: str) -> dict:
        """
        Return file changes and diffs between two commits.

        Args:
            from_commit: Source commit hash (newer).
            to_commit:   Target commit hash (older / base).

        Returns:
            Dict matching the shape of get_repo_changes output.
        """
        diff_name_cmd = f"git diff --name-only {to_commit}...{from_commit}"
        branch_files_raw, _ = exec_command(diff_name_cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
        branch_files = [f for f in branch_files_raw.strip().split("\n") if f]

        def get_file_diff(file_path: str) -> str:
            cmd = f"git diff {to_commit}...{from_commit} -- {file_path}"
            out, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            return out.strip()

        def get_file_commits(file_path: str) -> list:
            pretty = '{ "commit": "%H", "author": "%an", "date": "%as", "message": "%f" }'
            cmd = f"git log --pretty=format:'{pretty}' {to_commit}..{from_commit} -- {file_path}"
            out, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            results = []
            for line in out.strip().split("\n"):
                try:
                    results.append(json.loads(line))
                except Exception:
                    pass
            return results

        branch_file_and_commits = {
            file_path: {
                "commits": get_file_commits(file_path),
                "diff": get_file_diff(file_path),
                "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(file_path),
            }
            for file_path in branch_files
        }

        git_diff_cmd = f"git diff {to_commit} {from_commit}"
        git_diff_out, _ = exec_command(git_diff_cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
        git_diff_stat_out, _ = exec_command(
            f"git diff --shortstat {to_commit} {from_commit}",
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
        )

        pr_details = self.get_pr_review_details_by_commits(from_commit, to_commit)

        return {
            "diff": git_diff_out,
            "stat": git_diff_stat_out,
            "git_diff_cmd": git_diff_cmd,
            "local_changes": {},
            "repo_path": self.find_git_root_path(),
            "pr_details": pr_details,
            "commits": [],
            "branch_file_and_commits": branch_file_and_commits,
            "compare_type": "commit",
            "from_commit": from_commit,
            "to_commit": to_commit,
        }

    def get_pr_review_details_by_commits(self, from_commit: str, to_commit: str) -> list:
        """
        Return PR review details between two commits.

        Args:
            from_commit: Source commit hash.
            to_commit:   Target / base commit hash.

        Returns:
            List of change dicts per file.
        """
        diff_command = f"git diff --name-status {to_commit}..{from_commit}"
        stdout, _ = exec_command(diff_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)

        STATUS_MAP = {"A": "new", "D": "deleted"}
        changes = []

        for line in stdout.strip().split("\n"):
            # Guard: skip empty lines or lines without a tab separator
            if not line or "\t" not in line:
                continue
            parts = line.split("\t", 1)
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            status, file_path = parts
            file_path = file_path.strip()
            if not file_path:
                continue

            file_status = STATUS_MAP.get(status.strip(), "modified")

            file_diff, _ = exec_command(
                f"git diff {to_commit}..{from_commit} -- {file_path}",
                cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )
            file_commits_raw, _ = exec_command(
                f"git log --oneline {to_commit}..{from_commit} -- {file_path}",
                cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )
            changes.append({
                "file_name": file_path,
                "status": file_status,
                "diff": file_diff,
                "commits": [c for c in file_commits_raw.strip().split("\n") if c],
                "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(file_path),
            })

        return changes

    def get_repo_changes(self, from_branch: str, to_branch: str) -> dict:
        """
        Return file changes, diffs and PR details between two branches.
        Each file entry includes a 'last_modification' datetime (ISO 8601).
        """
        # Sanitize branch names
        from_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(from_branch)
        to_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(to_branch)
        
        is_current_branch = from_branch != to_branch  # Simplified check after sanitization

        # Get list of changed files
        git_branch_file_changed = f"git diff --name-only {to_branch}...{from_branch}"
        branch_files_output, _ = exec_command(
            git_branch_file_changed, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
        )
        branch_files = [f.strip() for f in branch_files_output.strip().split("\n") if f.strip()]

        def get_git_file_diff(file_path: str) -> str:
            """Get diff for a specific file between branches."""
            cmd = f"git diff {to_branch}...{from_branch} -- {file_path}"
            git_cmd_out, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            return git_cmd_out.strip()

        def get_git_file_commits(file_path: str) -> list:
            """Get commits that touched a specific file between branches."""
            pretty = '{ "commit": "%H", "author": "%an", "date": "%as", "message": "%f" }'
            cmd = f"git log --pretty=format:'{pretty}' {to_branch}..{from_branch} -- {file_path}"
            git_cmd_out, _ = exec_command(cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)
            
            results = []
            for line in git_cmd_out.strip().split("\n"):
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                try:
                    results.append(json.loads(line))
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.warning("Could not parse commit line for %s: %s", file_path, ex)
            return results

        # Build per-file metadata
        branch_file_and_commits = {}
        for file_path in branch_files:
            if not file_path:
                continue
            
            branch_file_and_commits[file_path] = {
                "commits": get_git_file_commits(file_path),
                "diff": get_git_file_diff(file_path),
                "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(file_path),
            }

        # Get overall diff stats
        git_diff_cmd = (
            f"git diff {to_branch} {from_branch}"
            if from_branch != "local"
            else f"git diff {to_branch}"
        )

        git_diff_cmd_out, _ = exec_command(
            git_diff_cmd, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
        )
        git_diff_cmd_stat_out, _ = exec_command(
            git_diff_cmd.replace("git diff", "git diff --shortstat"),
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )

        # Handle local changes if comparing against current branch
        local_changes: dict = {}
        if is_current_branch:
            git_local, _ = exec_command(
                "git status -s", cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )
            local_files = [f.strip().split(" ")[-1] for f in git_local.split("\n") if f.strip()]
            
            for file in local_files:
                full_path = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, file)
                if os.path.isfile(full_path):
                    git_diff_local_out, _ = exec_command(
                        f"git diff {to_branch} {file}",
                        cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
                    )
                    local_changes[file] = {
                        "diff": git_diff_local_out or (
                            f"diff --git a/ b/{file}\nnew file mode"
                        ),
                        "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(file),
                    }

            # Merge local changes into branch changes
            for local_file, local_file_info in local_changes.items():
                if local_file in branch_file_and_commits:
                    branch_file_and_commits[local_file]["diff"] = local_file_info["diff"]
                    branch_file_and_commits[local_file]["last_modification"] = (
                        local_file_info["last_modification"]
                    )
                else:
                    branch_file_and_commits[local_file] = local_file_info

        pr_details = self.get_pr_review_details(from_branch, to_branch)

        return {
            "diff": git_diff_cmd_out,
            "stat": git_diff_cmd_stat_out,
            "git_diff_cmd": git_diff_cmd,
            "local_changes": local_changes,
            "repo_path": self.find_git_root_path(),
            "pr_details": pr_details,
            "commits": [],
            "branch_file_and_commits": branch_file_and_commits,
            "compare_type": "branch",
        }

    def get_branch_commits(self, from_branch: str, repo_path: str) -> list:
        """
        Return structured commit list for a branch.
        """
        from_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(from_branch)
        git_log_command = (
            f"git log --pretty=format:%H|%an|%ae|%ad|%s {from_branch}"
        )
        stdout, _ = exec_command(git_log_command, cwd=repo_path)

        log_entries = stdout.strip().split("\n")
        log_list = []
        for entry in log_entries:
            if not entry.strip():
                continue
            commit_hash, author_name, author_email, date, message = entry.split("|", 4)
            log_list.append(
                {
                    "commit": commit_hash,
                    "author": {"name": author_name, "email": author_email},
                    "date": date,
                    "message": message.strip(),
                }
            )
        return log_list

    def get_repo_tree(self) -> list:
        """
        Build a full repo tree with branches and commits.
        """
        branches = self.get_repo_branches()
        repo_tree = []

        for branch in branches:
            branch_details = self.get_branch_details(branch_name=branch)
            branch_info = {
                "branch_name": branch,
                "author": "",
                "date": "",
                "commits": [],
            }
            for commit in branch_details["commits"]:
                branch_info["commits"].append(
                    {
                        "commit_id": commit["commit_hash"],
                        "author": commit["author"],
                        "date": commit["date"],
                        "comment": commit["message"],
                        "files": commit["files"],
                    }
                )
            repo_tree.append(branch_info)

        return repo_tree

    def get_branch_details(self, branch_name: str) -> dict:
        """
        Extract commit details from a branch without checking it out.
        """
        branch_name = self._sanitize_branch_name(branch_name)
        log_command = f"git log -g --format=%H|%an|%cI|%s {branch_name}"
        stdout, _ = exec_command(log_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)

        log_lines = stdout.split("\n")
        commits = []

        for entry in log_lines:
            if not entry.strip():
                continue
            try:
                commit_hash, author, date, message = entry.split("|", 3)
            except ValueError:
                continue

            file_changes_command = (
                f"git show --name-only --pretty=format:{commit_hash}"
            )
            stdout_files, _ = exec_command(
                file_changes_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )
            file_changes = stdout_files.strip().split("\n")

            enriched_files = []
            for f in file_changes[1:]:
                if not f:
                    continue
                enriched_files.append(
                    {
                        "file_path": f,
                        "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(f),
                    }
                )

            commits.append(
                {
                    "entry_line": entry,
                    "commit_hash": commit_hash,
                    "author": author,
                    "date": date,
                    "message": message,
                    "files": enriched_files,
                }
            )

        return {
            "commits": commits,
            "parent_branch": commits[-1]["commit_hash"] if commits else None,
        }

    def get_project_current_branch(self) -> str:
        """Return the current git branch name."""
        stdout, _ = exec_command(
            "git branch --show-current", cwd=self._get_repo_root()
        )
        return stdout.strip()

    def get_project_parent_branch(self) -> str:
        """Determine the parent branch of the current branch via reflog."""
        current_branch = self.get_project_current_branch()
        stdout, _ = exec_command(
            f"git reflog {current_branch}",
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )
        self.session.log_info(
            "get_project_parent_branch reflog: %s cwd: %s",
            stdout,
            self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )

        creation_lines = [l for l in stdout.split("\n") if "Created from" in l]
        if not creation_lines:
            return ""

        creation_line = creation_lines[0]

        if "refs/remotes/" in creation_line:
            ref_branch = creation_line.split(" ")[-1].replace("refs/remotes/", "")
            return self._sanitize_branch_name(ref_branch)

        ref_branch = creation_line.split(" (")[1].split(",")[0]
        return self._sanitize_branch_name(ref_branch)

    def get_project_changes(self, parent_branch: str = None) -> dict:
        """Return diff between current working tree and a parent branch."""
        if not parent_branch:
            parent_branch = "HEAD@{1}"
            self.session.log_info(
                "get_project_changes parent_branch %s", parent_branch
            )

        diff_out, _ = exec_command(
            f"git diff {parent_branch}", cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
        )
        diff_stat_out, _ = exec_command(
            f"git diff --shortstat {parent_branch}",
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )
        return {"diff": diff_out, "stats": diff_stat_out}

    def build_code_changes_summary(self, force: bool = False) -> object:
        """Build a code changes summary from git diff."""
        project_branches = self.get_project_branches()
        diff = project_branches.get("git_diff", "")
        return self.session.get_knowledge().build_code_changes_summary(
            diff=diff, force=force
        )

    def get_pr_review_details(self, from_branch: str, to_branch: str) -> list:
        """
        Return PR review details (file changes, diffs, commits) between two branches.
        Each file entry includes a 'last_modification' datetime (ISO 8601).
        """
        # Sanitize branch names
        from_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(from_branch)
        to_branch = self._sanitize_branch_name(to_branch)
        
        exec_command(
            f"git fetch origin {to_branch}:{to_branch}",
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )
        exec_command(
            f"git fetch origin {from_branch}:{from_branch}",
            cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path,
        )

        diff_command = f"git diff --name-status {to_branch}..{from_branch}"
        stdout, _ = exec_command(diff_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path)

        STATUS_MAP = {"A": "new", "D": "deleted"}
        changes = []

        for line in stdout.strip().split("\n"):
            # Guard: skip empty or tab-less lines to avoid unpack errors
            if not line or "\t" not in line:
                continue
            parts = line.split("\t", 1)
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            status, file_path = parts
            file_path = file_path.strip()
            if not file_path:
                continue

            file_status = STATUS_MAP.get(status.strip(), "modified")

            file_diff_command = f"git diff {to_branch}..{from_branch} -- {file_path}"
            file_diff, _ = exec_command(
                file_diff_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )

            file_commits_command = (
                f"git log --oneline {to_branch}..{from_branch} -- {file_path}"
            )
            file_commits_stdout, _ = exec_command(
                file_commits_command, cwd=self.settings.abs_project_path
            )
            file_commits = [c for c in file_commits_stdout.strip().split("\n") if c]

            changes.append(
                {
                    "file_name": file_path,
                    "status": file_status,
                    "diff": file_diff,
                    "commits": file_commits,
                    "last_modification": self._get_file_last_modification(file_path),
                }
            )

        return changes

    def _clean_status_path(self, path: str) -> str:
        """
        Return the target path of a porcelain status entry.

        Rename entries keep only the destination path and quoted paths (paths
        with spaces or special characters) are unquoted.

        Args:
            path: Raw path read from ``git status --porcelain``.

        Returns:
            Cleaned, repo-relative file path.
        """
        path = (path or "").strip()
        if " -> " in path:
            path = path.split(" -> ")[-1].strip()
        return path.strip('"')

    def _parse_status_line(self, line: str) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
        """
        Split a porcelain v1 status line into its parts.

        The format is ``XY <path>``: X is the staged (index) status and Y the
        unstaged (worktree) status. The leading space of a line may have been
        trimmed when reading the command output, so the separator position is
        used to detect the shifted format.

        Args:
            line: One line of ``git status --porcelain`` output.

        Returns:
            Tuple of ``(index_code, worktree_code, path)``, or None when the
            line has no usable entry.
        """
        if not line or not line.strip():
            return None

        if len(line) >= 3 and line[2] == " ":
            index_code, worktree_code, path = line[0], line[1], line[3:]
        elif len(line) >= 2:
            # Leading space was trimmed: only the worktree status is left
            index_code, worktree_code, path = " ", line[0], line[2:]
        else:
            return None

        path = self._clean_status_path(path)
        if not path:
            return None
        return index_code, worktree_code, path

    def _status_entry(self, code: str, path: str) -> dict:
        """
        Build a staged/unstaged status entry.

        Args:
            code: Porcelain status code (``M``, ``A``, ``D``, ``?``...).
            path: Repo-relative file path.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'path', 'code' and 'status'.
        """
        return {
            "path": path,
            "code": code,
            "status": PORCELAIN_STATUS.get(code, "modified"),
        }

    def _status_paths(self, cwd: Optional[str] = None) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the paths currently reported by ``git status --porcelain``.

        Ignored files (``!`` entries) are skipped: they cannot be staged.

        Args:
            cwd: Working directory. Defaults to the repository root.

        Returns:
            De-duplicated, repo-relative paths.

        Example:
            >>> engine._status_paths()
            ['app.py', 'new.json']
        """
        result = self._run_git(["status", "--porcelain"], cwd=cwd, strip_output=False)
        paths: List[str] = []

        for line in result["output"].split("\n"):
            parsed = self._parse_status_line(line)
            if not parsed:
                continue
            index_code, worktree_code, path = parsed
            if index_code == "!" or worktree_code == "!":
                continue
            if path not in paths:
                paths.append(path)

        return paths

    def get_status_changes(self, files: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> dict:
        """
        Split the working tree status into staged and unstaged file lists.

        Args:
            files: Porcelain status lines. Read from git when omitted.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'staged' and 'unstaged' lists of
            ``{path, code, status}`` entries.

        Example:
            >>> engine.get_status_changes()
            {'staged': [{'path': 'app.py', 'code': 'M', 'status': 'modified'}],
             'unstaged': [{'path': 'new.json', 'code': '?', 'status': 'untracked'}]}
        """
        if files is None:
            files = self.get_working_tree_status()["files"]

        staged: List[dict] = []
        unstaged: List[dict] = []

        for line in files:
            parsed = self._parse_status_line(line)
            if not parsed:
                continue

            index_code, worktree_code, path = parsed

            # '!' entries are ignored files: never shown as changes
            if index_code == "!" or worktree_code == "!":
                continue

            if index_code == "?" and worktree_code == "?":
                unstaged.append(self._status_entry("?", path))
                continue

            if index_code != " ":
                staged.append(self._status_entry(index_code, path))
            if worktree_code not in (" ", "?"):
                unstaged.append(self._status_entry(worktree_code, path))

        return {"staged": staged, "unstaged": unstaged}

    def get_working_tree_status(self) -> dict:
        """
        Return the working tree status of the repository.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'ok', 'dirty', 'files' (porcelain lines) and 'error'.

        Example:
            >>> engine.get_working_tree_status()
            {'ok': True, 'dirty': True, 'files': [' M codx/junior/app.py'], 'error': ''}
        """
        # Leading spaces are part of the porcelain format (index vs worktree)
        result = self._run_git(["status", "--porcelain"], strip_output=False)
        files = [line for line in result["output"].split("\n") if line.strip()]
        return {
            "ok": result["ok"],
            "dirty": bool(files),
